doc.title: Donn Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 6, 2009

title: Drummers Skooky Sherman, Ronnie Zito and Jimmy Wormworth
summary: The band's drummers over the years and their later professional careers.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: So who was your drummer mostly during those years?

Skooky Sherman was the first one, and then he graduated, and then for the times after that we were fortunate to be able to use two drummers from Utica. One of them, I think the first kid was Ronnie Zito who went on, he’s now a studio musician and worked with Woody Herman, a wonderful, wonderful drummer. And we couldn’t get him for a gig, and he says, “Well I’ve got this other fella, his name is Jimmy Wormworth, and he’d be more than happy to do it.” So we started alternating, you know, using them both. And then when it came time to go to Europe, Ronnie’s father was afraid that he was going to — he was sick. He was afraid he was going to pass away while he was in Europe, and then Ronnie wouldn’t be able to get home for, whatever. So Ronnie couldn’t go to Europe so we took Jimmy. And Jimmy also played with us in Carnegie Hall. And then they both went on the professional careers. Jimmy is still, well both of them are still playing. Jimmy ended up with Lambert, Hendricks & Ross and the Ike Isaacs Trio, and now he works around New York, most recently he did a European tour with Annie Ross.
That’s great. He talked about that, that little stint with you guys on the ship and everything.
